subject: biology-2
question: Scientists are monitoring an **emerging virus** that recently jumped from an animal reservoir into humans. Which factor would most directly drive this virus to spread rapidly through the human population?

options.text: The virus infects only one person and never passes from person to person.
The virus has a genome identical to every other known virus.
The virus is quickly destroyed by the normal temperature of the human body.
The virus mutates often and gains the ability to transmit between humans while evading their immunity.

explanation: Emerging viruses typically spill over from animal reservoirs, mutate to evade immunity, and gain efficient person to person transmission. A, B, and C all describe viruses that would fail to spread, because they never pass between hosts, offer nothing new, or cannot survive in the body.
